newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares closer lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares closer lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange receded further at close on Monday on profit-taking by investors and speculators, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 12.62 points lower at 689.53 points.
"The fall in the share prices was a technical correction as the market is in an overbought position in the short run," said S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit.
Brokers said profit-taking in the wake of Monday's gains dominated the trading, but market sentiment could pick up if the government intervened with some market friendly measures.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was meeting country's leading industrialists and economists on Tuesday to discuss ways to boost economy.
Traders said most investors were not interested in enlarging their positions on the last day of the year and kept to the sidelines.
Brokers said automobile companies led the fall with TELCO dropping 9.95 rupees to 344.0 on heavy selling by speculators.
Bajaj Auto closed 21.0 rupees lower at 907.0 on profit-taking.
Cement-maker ACC dropped 23.05 rupees to 1,252.0 and Reliance Industries ended 2.20 rupees lower at 208.35 following sustained selling pressure from speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India slipped 2.35 rupees to 236.15 on selective selling by financial institutions, they said.
